transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Lumen Head of ML), Evan Ross (Platform Eng), Sarah Lim (PM)

Summary:
Quick product walkthrough of EvalOps (prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B compare) focused on Lumen's use case for clinical triage assistant. Discussed signal collection, alert thresholds, secure private deployment options (VPC, KMS), and a proposed pilot with scheduled benchmarks. Agreed next steps around security docs, sandbox access, and benchmark window.

Topics covered:
- Prompt set design and versioning
- Regression alerting and triage workflow
- A/B comparison methodology and metrics (accuracy, hallucination rate, latency)
- Private deployment concerns: VPC peering, KMS, audit logs
- Demo of Console: prompt set UI, evaluation runs, alert config templates

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you carving out time. Quick round robin, and then we'll jump into the console.
[00:08] Priya Kapoor: Hi Maya, Priya here. I'm the head of ML at Lumen, we own the triage models that power the chatbot. Evan and Sarah are with me.
[00:14] Evan Ross: Evan, platform eng. we'll need to make sure networking and keys are ok.
[00:18] Sarah Lim: Sarah, product. Focused on user flows and regression impact to SLAs.
[00:22] Maya Chen: Great. Diego from my side will drive the demo, I'll cover procurement and pricing questions after.
[00:28] Diego Alvarez: Cool, I'm going to share my screen — tell me if you see the console.
[00:32] [screen share noise]
[00:36] Diego Alvarez: Alright this first tab is the prompt sets workspace. You can see we've uploaded a sample CSV of 2k prompts for clinical triage, each row has expected label, confidence buckets and a reference answer. We version prompt sets, so if you update templates you get a immutable snapshot.
[01:05] Priya Kapoor: Quick question — is the reference answer stored in Redwood? We have patient PII concerns.
[01:12] Diego Alvarez: Good call. By default reference artifacts are stored in encrypted blob store, and for Private deployments you can configure customer-managed KMS or HSM. There's also a toggle to redact PII before storage but that impacts eval fidelity.
[01:26] Sarah Lim: That redact toggle — does it strip PHI from the prompt itself or the model output?
[01:32] Diego Alvarez: Both, it's a preprocessing hook. It will mask patterns we detect (names, MRNs), but again depending on your eval you might want raw text in a private VPC option.
[01:42] Evan Ross: So for private we get VPC peering and KMS — and audit logs?
[01:46] Maya Chen: Yep, private includes a customer-controlled control-plane, VPC peering, KMS integration and audit logs with retention policies you can set. We can include an architecture appendix in the follow up.
[01:56] Priya Kapoor: Ok good. On the regression alerts — show us how that works. We need early heads-up when accuracy drops or hallucinations spike.
[02:04] Diego Alvarez: Sure. I'll run an evaluation now against the "triage-v1" prompt set. I'm going to kick off a batch eval, you can see metrics streaming — accuracy, token-level hallucination score, and a custom FNR metric you can add.
[02:24] [eval job runs — console refresh chime]
[02:27] Diego Alvarez: So here's a run. We set baseline thresholds, which we recommend: 1) accuracy decrease > 3% over a rolling 7-day window, 2) hallucination rate > 2% absolute. When thresholds breach you get an alert to email/Slack, and an automated regression ticket with relevant sample prompts.
[02:50] Priya Kapoor: Do the alerts include model + quantization variant? Our prod is on a quantized 4-bit variant and sometimes performance differences pop up there.
[02:58] Diego Alvarez: Yeah, runs tag model name, version, quantization and hardware runtime. If you use our smart routing we also capture which variant served the request.
[03:10] Sarah Lim: Can we route alerts to PagerDuty? We need immediate ops visibility for high-severity regressions.
[03:15] Maya Chen: PagerDuty and webhooks are supported. You can map severity levels to escalation policies.
[03:21] Evan Ross: On A/B comparisons — we have two candidate finetunes, one with instruction-tuning and one with external KB. We want to run A/B across traffic and also offline evals. How does Redwood handle comparing samples?
[03:33] Diego Alvarez: Two ways: offline A/B in the console — run paired evaluations on the same prompt set and use paired metrics (Delta accuracy, BLEU-like, and custom quality rubric). For online A/B we can split traffic by route or model variant and collect online labels via human raters or automatic heuristics. Console shows pairwise view with side-by-side outputs and an aggregate significance test.
[03:52] Priya Kapoor: Significance test — is that a simple t-test or something fancier? We need non-parametric because our labels aren't gaussian.
[03:58] Diego Alvarez: We offer bootstrap resampling by default and you can export raw predictions for your own stats.
[04:06] [background mutter]
[04:10] Priya Kapoor: Walk me through an alert drill — how do we triage?
[04:13] Diego Alvarez: When an alert fires you first get a triage view: top failing prompts, model metadata (runtime, quantization), diffs from previous run, and a suggested rollback if severity is critical. The playbook links to your runbook in Confluence and can create a Jira ticket prefilled with sample prompts and suggested mitigations (hotfix prompt, revert model, tweak decoding).
[04:37] Sarah Lim: Nice. Any false-positive rate on hallucination detection? We worry about noise.
[04:42] Diego Alvarez: Hallucination detection is noisy — we provide confidence bands and threshold tuning. Many customers set a two-stage alert: low-confidence informational alert then a second critical threshold.
[04:55] Evan Ross: For the pilot we probably want to run against a mirror of production traffic. How does data capture work? We need KV cache and prefix caching to not distort latency during the benchmark.
[05:05] Diego Alvarez: For benchmarking we recommend a replay using the same sequence lengths and KV cache warmup. Our runner includes options to replay with/without KV cache to measure realistic latency. The runtime exposes per-token latency and batch size stats.
[05:20] Priya Kapoor: Can we simulate slow tails — like 95th percentile spikes?
[05:23] Diego Alvarez: Yes the dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 and you can inject synthetic heavy tails in the runner.
[05:29] [pause, coughing, small cross talk]
[05:35] Maya Chen: I want to highlight pricing models for the pilot — eval runs charge per token + an evaluation compute surcharge for large batches if you use hosted. If you go Dedicated or Private there are reserved capacity options we can price out. I'll follow up with a price estimate for your projected 3-month pilot.
[05:54] Priya Kapoor: Sounds good — given our compliance needs we might lean Private, but we want to see the eval workflow first.
[06:00] Diego Alvarez: I'll walk through the A/B compare UI — quick demo: select two runs, pick a scoring rubric. Here's a pairwise diff view. You can filter by label type and severity, and pin problem prompts to an investigation board.
[06:20] [diego clicks]
[06:24] Diego Alvarez: See here, this prompt shows the candidate model hallucinated a drug dosage. It's flagged and we attach the full input + model outputs + token-level attention heatmap — though the attention view is approximate.
[06:38] Priya Kapoor: The drug dosage hallucination is exactly our nightmare scenario. Is there an automated suppress-for-production rule?
[06:44] Diego Alvarez: You can define guardrail rules that trigger either a rejection or a safe-response template. Those rules are enforced at inference time via an inline filter. They can also be set to only alert during eval.
[06:57] Evan Ross: Technical question: when we run evals in our VPC, is the data ever egressed to Redwood-hosted compute? We need assurance for PHI.
[07:06] Maya Chen: In a Private on-prem deployment, no. For VPC-hosted private we do control-plane coordination but data path can be configured to stay within your network via private peering. We'll send details in the architecture appendix.
[07:18] Sarah Lim: Ok, last piece — how do we instrument human labels for online A/B? We expect to have clinicians rate a smallish sample.
[07:25] Diego Alvarez: There's a lightweight labelling UI you can embed for raters, or we can integrate with your existing workflow through webhooks and a CSV export. We also provide QC metrics for inter-rater agreement.
[07:36] Priya Kapoor: Good. I'd like to pilot with 10k prompts offline and a 48-hour online shadow test. We can confirm specifics after we get the sandbox.
[07:44] Maya Chen: Perfect — we'll package the SOC2 and architecture appendix and Diego will share sandbox creds. Any other questions?
[07:52] Evan Ross: One more — what about SSO? We need SAML and SCIM for user provisioning.
[07:57] Maya Chen: SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning supported for all plans, and RBAC integration. We'll include SAML metadata in the follow-up.
[08:07] [wrap-up]
[08:10] Maya Chen: Recap of next steps: security pack + SAML metadata (Maya), sandbox creds + prompt set template (Diego), confirm benchmark dataset (Priya). We'll aim to reconvene after sandbox validation. Thanks all.

End of transcript.
